title: Atoi
instructions: Write a function that simulates the behaviour of the Atoi function in Go.
Atoi transforms a number represented as a string into a number represented as an int.
Atoi returns 0 if the string is not considered as a valid number.
Non-valid string chains will be tested — some will contain non-digit characters.
The handling of the signs + or - does have to be taken into account.
This function will only have to return the int — the error result of Atoi is not required.
testTemplate:
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"piscine"
)

func main() {
	fmt.Println(piscine.Atoi("12345"))
	fmt.Println(piscine.Atoi("0000000012345"))
	fmt.Println(piscine.Atoi("012 345"))
	fmt.Println(piscine.Atoi("Hello World!"))
	fmt.Println(piscine.Atoi("+1234"))
	fmt.Println(piscine.Atoi("-1234"))
	fmt.Println(piscine.Atoi("++1234"))
	fmt.Println(piscine.Atoi("--1234"))
}

title: Fibonacci
instructions: Write a recursive function that returns the value at the position index in the fibonacci sequence.
The first value is at index 0.
The sequence starts this way: 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8...
A negative index will return -1.
for loops are forbidden for this exercise — use recursion only.

title: IsPrime
instructions: Write a function called IsPrime() that checks if a given integer is a prime number.
The function should return true if the number is prime, and false otherwise.
Negative numbers, 0, and 1 are not prime numbers.

Your solution file must also include a helper IsEven function: func IsEven(n int) bool that returns true if n is even.

title: CamelToSnakeCase
instructions: Write a function that converts a string from camelCase to snake_case.
If the string is empty, return an empty string.
If the string is not camelCase, return the string unchanged.
Rules for writing in camelCase:
The word does not end on a capitalized letter (CamelCasE is invalid).
No two capitalized letters shall follow directly each other (CamelCAse is invalid).
Numbers or punctuation are not allowed in the word anywhere (camelCase1 is invalid).

title: CheckNumber

title: HashCode
instructions: Write a function called HashCode() that takes a string as an argument and returns a new hashed string.
The hash equation is computed as follows: (ASCII of current character + size of the string) % 127.
If the resulting character is unprintable (below ASCII 32), add 33 to it.

title: PrintComb
instructions: Write a function that prints, in ascending order and on a single line, all unique combinations of three different digits so that the first digit is lower than the second, and the second is lower than the third.
These combinations are separated by a comma and a space.
000 or 999 are not valid combinations because the digits are not different.
987 should not be shown because the first digit is not less than the second.

title: printrevcomb

These combinations are separated by a comma and a space.
999 or 000 are not valid combinations because the digits are not different.
789 should not be shown because the first digit is not greater than the second.

title: ItoaBase
instructions: Write a function that converts an int value to a string using the specified base and returns this string.
The base is expressed as an int, from 2 to 16.
The characters comprising the base are the digits 0 to 9, followed by uppercase letters A to F.
For example, base 4 is equivalent to '0123' and base 16 is '0123456789ABCDEF'.
If the value is negative, the resulting string must be preceded by a minus sign -.

title: alphamirror
instructions: Write a program called alphamirror that takes a string as argument and displays this string after replacing each alphabetical character with the opposite alphabetical character.
The case of the letter remains unchanged: 'a' becomes 'z', 'Z' becomes 'A', 'd' becomes 'w', 'M' becomes 'N'.
The final result is followed by a newline.
If the number of arguments is different from 1, the program prints a new line.

title: switchcase

The result must be followed by a newline.

title: ispowerof2
instructions: Write a program that determines if a given number is a power of 2.
A number n is a power of 2 if n = 2^m where m is another integer.
Print true if the given number is a power of 2, otherwise print false.
If there is more than one or no argument, the program should print nothing.
When there is only one argument, it will always be a positive valid int.

title: addprimesum
instructions: Write a program that takes a positive integer as argument and displays the sum of all prime numbers less than or equal to it, followed by a newline.
If the number of arguments is different from 1, or if the argument is not a positive number, the program displays 0 followed by a newline.
